title: Boundary replacement and extension of subdivisions
as_he_states: A subdivision prescribed on a subfigure should extend to the whole figure, and compatible induced refinements should agree.
plausible_today: The explicit family G′∪(F minus G) is invalid for abstract augmented strata but valid for V’s concrete subsets; the abstract theorem is existential and may replace larger strata.
state_of_art: No exact later theorem for the abstract package located; V30–45 is the internal concrete repair.
why_open: IV45–48 exposes the boundary obstruction and explicitly corrects the construction.
worth: Yes: construct one fully specified non-set model in which the existential extension axiom can be verified.

title: Booleanity of virtual supports
as_he_states: The biorthogonal virtual-support lattice should be a complete Boolean algebra and yield an ultrastonian space.
plausible_today: It is generally a complete ortholattice, with Booleanity requiring additional distributivity.
state_of_art: Hua2026 §79 is an exact negative answer; this run verifies the full finite figure hypotheses in seven- and ten-element models.
why_open: IV69 states the presumption and the missing distributive identity; no historical account of abandonment located.
worth: Yes: characterize additional geometric axioms forcing distributivity, rather than reproving the false conjecture.

title: Extending a subdivision with unchanged exterior
as_he_states: Extend G′≼G≤F to F′≼F; preferably leave exterior strata unchanged and obtain a canonical/least extension, or one elementary filler for a subdivided boundary.
plausible_today: Separate existence of an extension in a specified PL/semianalytic category from uniqueness and unchanged incidence. A strict simplicial elementary filler fails for a triangle with a subdivided edge. Any elementary-boundary uniqueness statement needs fixed support and an equivalence convention.
state_of_art: Łojasiewicz1964 §3 Theorems1–2 pp463–464 proves simultaneous locally finite triangulation of locally finite semianalytic families. Baro2010 Theorem4.3 proves compatible normal triangulation for a closed finite definable complex. Neither asserts the exact unchanged-exterior/unique-elementary extension requested here.
why_open: The author explicitly sees failure for strict simplicial ateliers and calls these axioms optional. No later source explains a historical abandonment.
worth: Worth reformulating only after choosing the geometric category; a few-hour task can test precise relative versions, not promise canonical uniqueness.

title: What algebraic structure do virtual supports have?
as_he_states: Are orthoclosed virtual supports distributive, and does empty intersection with a cosupport imply containment?
plausible_today: In general they form a complete ortholattice. Orthomodularity and Boolean distributivity are extra properties. Under L2 plus a complete distinct-locus orthogonality graph the lattice is P(L), but this special case does not generalize.
state_of_art: Lindenhovius–Vetterlein2023 Example3.3 gives the exact six-element nonorthomodular P4 support lattice; Lemma3.4 states the Dacey criterion for orthomodularity. Janowitz1963 p1241 verifies the older orthomodular identity.
why_open: The manuscript later computes counterexamples and abandons the blanket Boolean expectation; there is no evidence that the general claim remained an open theorem.
worth: Worth classifying additional geometric hypotheses only; the unconditional Boolean question is already answered negatively.

title: Existence of support realizations and redundancy of axioms
as_he_states: Find P with support subsets satisfying clauses(i)–(vi), and decide which compatibility, subdivision, lieu and separation clauses follow from the others.
plausible_today: Exact disjointness plus singleton support for every p yields Σ≅P(P), but does not construct such a realization from an arbitrary atelier. Redundancy of geometric clauses needs explicit incidence/refinement arguments beyond the Boolean lattice.
state_of_art: Massas2023 Theorem2.29 gives the complete atomic Boolean/powerset equivalence. Lindenhovius–Vetterlein2023 Example3.3 blocks a universal Boolean realization for arbitrary orthogonality spaces. No exact theorem settling all six atelier clauses was found in S67-01,07,09–12.
why_open: The pages prove implications under Hyp/Hyp′ and then say the remaining clauses are presumed; the two-strand margin exposes a failure of Supp1 in a tempting example.
worth: Worth an axiom-independence table; begin with the proven singleton theorem and separate the unproved existence step.

title: Representing supports by sets
as_he_states: Find support functions and decide whether support inclusion recovers the face order.
plausible_today: Under the partition condition the incidence-reflection lemma is proved here; existence and universality of a sufficiently faithful support representation require the later disjunctor construction.
state_of_art: As of19November2026: The incidence-reflection result under the least-membership/partition assumptions is proved on VIII42–52. Birkhoff1948 IV§§5–6 gives the general closed-set support lattice, and Paseka–Vetterlein2025 Proposition2.4 gives join-dense ortholattice representation. These do not ensure a faithful realization into ordinary set figures with all incidence/refinement relations reflected. The source later moves to abstract spatios.
why_open: The supplied text records a task or uncertainty; no external source documenting why it was left open has been found.
worth: Worth separating set realization from ortholattice realization, because the latter has a precise theorem while the former requires extra geometric information.

title: Functoriality of orthogonality support completion
as_he_states: Disjointness compatibility does not prove the essential support/complement formulas; correction needed.
plausible_today: For disjoncteurs E,F and alpha:E→P(F), write c_E,c_F for double-polar closure, alpha_bar(A)=union_{x in A}alpha(x), and f(S)=c_F(alpha_bar(S)) on closed S. Then alpha has a pretranspose iff c_F alpha_bar c_E=c_F alpha_bar on every subset iff each orthogonality fiber {x:alpha(x) orthogonal y} is c_E-closed iff f preserves all joins, including the empty join, and f(c_E{x})=c_F(alpha(x)) for every x. The extra generator equality cannot be dropped; this criterion does not imply complement preservation.
state_of_art: As of19November2026: The unrestricted closure formula fails by C-SA21-9-030R; the author’s nonsurjective injection refutes the stronger complement formula only. The author subsequently repairs the criterion in Proposition4, IX95–97: for any correspondence alpha:E→P(F), pretranspose existence, commutation with double-polar closure on every subset, closed orthogonality fibers, and preservation of arbitrary joins PLUS alpha*(cl_E{x})=cl_F(alpha(x)) for every x are equivalent. The inserted generator condition is at J156-9-12:253–257 and is explicitly acknowledged as an afterthought at351–355; the complete argument at242–355 has now been checked directly. See C-SA21-9-038/054 and MP-SA21-9-10 for the continuation. Paseka–Vetterlein2025 Definition3.1, Lemmas3.5–3.7 and Theorem6.7 supply a later comparison for adjointable single-valued maps, not an automatic identification of the full atelier-morphism theory. This is an internally answered question after correction, not a still-unread continuation.
why_open: The early proof is crossed out on IX63–64; the stronger formula fails on IX65. Proposition4 on IX95–97 supplies the missing generator hypothesis and completes the corrected equivalence.
worth: Worth comparing the corrected correspondence criterion with later adjointability, while retaining the independent distinction between closure commutation, preservation of joins and preservation of complement.

title: When does a raw correspondence commute with support closure and admit a pretranspose?
occurrences: crosslink: MP-SA21-9-08 from IX01–08; earlier formula(*) is the same closure issue
as_he_states: Does cFᾱcE(A)=cFᾱ(A) hold, and does its validity for every A characterize disjunctive correspondences? Can a reverse correspondence β satisfy α(x)⊥y iff x⊥β(y)? The marginal alternatives ask for closed membership fibers and closed γ(y).
plausible_today: Exactly the equivalent conditions of corrected Proposition4: full closure commutation; a pretranspose; closed γ(y); inverse closed-membership fibers; or join preservation of fα together with fασE=cFα. Join preservation alone is insufficient. Every closed-valued compatible assignment comes from a unique join map.
state_of_art: C-SA21-9-033/035/036/038/054, proofsP2–P4. Shmuely1974 gives the complete-lattice Galois background; DomenachLeclerc2001 Theorems4.1/5.1 provide the arbitrary closure-presentation correspondence; PasekaVetterlein2025 Lemmas3.5–3.7 give a modern point-adjoint comparison.
why_open: The author initially confuses arbitrary generator assignments with compatible ones, then inserts the missing equality and explicitly acknowledges that addition on scan97. This is a documented internal correction, not a problem left unresolved at the end of these pages.
worth: The corrected theorem is settled; the useful next work is a source-critical exposition that retains the cancelled and corrected formulations.
